subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Drum vs. Fluid-Bed Roasters
description: A quick, practical guide to Drum vs. Fluid-Bed Roasters.

hook.text: Drum roasters tumble beans in a heated cylinder. Fluid-bed roasters suspend beans on a jet of hot air.

buildup.text: Drum roasters are the industry standard—they combine conduction and convection for rich, full-bodied results.

discovery.text: Fluid-bed roasters use pure convection. They produce cleaner, brighter cups with more distinct origin flavors.

twist.text: Fluid-bed roasts faster (8–12 minutes vs. 12–16 for drums) but is harder to control. Seconds of error cause bigger defects.

climax.text: Most specialty roasters use drums. But innovators like Sivetz championed fluid-bed for objectively cleaner coffee.

punchline.text: Drum for body, fluid-bed for clarity. The machine shapes the cup.

quiz.question: How does a fluid-bed roaster work?
options: Beans tumble in a heated cylinder
Beans are suspended on a jet of hot air for pure convection roasting
Beans are immersed in hot oil

details.summary: Drum roasters tumble beans inside a heated rotating cylinder, using a mix of conduction and convection. Fluid bed roasters levitate beans on a stream of hot air for purely convective heat transfer. Each design creates a distinct flavor profile and workflow.
details.whyItMatters: The choice of roaster type fundamentally shapes the flavor, consistency, and capacity of a roasting operation. Understanding both helps buyers and roasters make informed decisions.
takeaways: Drum roasters use conduction and convection in a rotating cylinder
Fluid bed roasters suspend beans on hot air for even heating
Drum roasts tend toward heavier body; fluid bed toward brighter acidity

faq.question: Which roaster type is more common in commercial specialty coffee?
faq.answer: Drum roasters dominate the specialty coffee industry due to their versatility, larger batch capacity, and the body-forward profiles they produce. Fluid bed roasters are popular for sample roasting and smaller operations.

faq.question: Are fluid bed roasters faster than drum roasters?
faq.answer: Generally yes. Because hot air contacts every bean surface simultaneously, fluid bed roasters often complete a batch in six to eight minutes compared to ten to fourteen minutes for a drum roaster.
